newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Standard arms for foreign competition.
newsitem.headline: Standard arms for foreign competition.

text.p: Fundamental organisational changes are being put in place at South Africa's Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd to equip the group for increased foreign competition, chairman Conrad Strauss said on Tuesday.

Strauss said in the banking group's annual review that although South Africa's banking and financial services industry was generally seen as its most globally competitive business sector, there was room for improvement.
"By international standards...South African banks' cost structures and manning levels are too high," he said.

Standard underwent a major restructure in 1995 when it was shaped into four main business units. A further series of re-engineering initiatives to improve operational efficiency and customer service standards were ongoing, Strauss said.
"These programmes...are progressing well and I have every confidence that their benefits will become evident in 1997."

Dozens of foreign banks have opened shop in South Africa since the first democratic elections in 1994, stealing business away from local operations especially in the corporate and merchant banking area.

Strauss said government's commitment to its macroeconomic programme, a five-year economic blueprint unveiled last June, was becoming more evident but that it would be more difficult to implement this year amid a slowing down in economic activity.
Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said earlier this month that the economy was expected to grow by 2.5 percent this year, down from 3.1 percent in 1996.
Other factors which would weigh on the country this year was the "unresolved dilemma" of foreign exchange control as well as continued high levels of crime, he said.
